text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Previously confidential documents obtained by the newspaper show that the central bank's defence of the Swedish crown for just one day in November, 1992, when the country was facing a currency crisis, cost the state at least five billion crowns.

- Sweden's involvement with the Baltic nations and Baltic Sea security has increased the possibility of a visit by U.S. President Bill Clinton in the middle of next year, the paper said. No sitting U.S. President has visited Sweden before.

- U.S./Swedish drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn will create about 100 new jobs in Stockholm with its plans for a new state-of-the-art research centre in the Kungsholmen district of the city, bringing together current facilities in Stockholm and Uppsala.

- Swedish exports increased by just one percent in current prices in the first 10 months of this year, according to the Export Council. Exports were impacted by a weaker business cycle and stronger crown.
- The Swedish government is planning to take control of electricity exports and imports which was previously a free market. This comes in a plan by Energy Minister Anders Sundstrom.

- The board of forestry company MoDo said the company's factory at Domsjo will not be sold. The company is currently reviewing its operations at Domsjo and Husum and will make a final decision in the autumn of 1998.

- Swedes have bought more overseas shares this year than foreign investors have bought in Sweden, the Stockholm stock exchange said. Even though increasing numbers of offshore investors are buying Swedish shares, Swedes are more active overseas and the trend appears set to continue.

- Volvo Aero and Daimler-Benz Aerosapce signed a Memorandum of Understanding on closer cooperation in the field of aero engines. The project is worth $600 million over a 20-year period. The companies expect to achieve substantial cost savings but will retain their technological core activities.

- Swedish consumers are rushing the pharmacies as the new year deadline for subscription charge increases approaches. One pharmacy in Stockholm had to close its doors for two hours on Wednesday to give staff time to process subscriptions.
- Denmark's Egmont has replaced Bonnier-owned SF as 20th Century Fox's Scandinavian distributor of videos for sale and rental. Fox video distribution has an annual turnover of 50 million crowns.
